themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 64 THIS WEEK, a 341% spike above the 8-week baseline of 14.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 8.46), suggesting rapid deterioration across neighborhood roads at the same moment DOT roadway maintenance appears on repeat budget requests.
evidence: 64 street condition complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 14.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (341% increase, z-score 8.46)
Street/roadway maintenance listed as standing budget request across multiple fiscal years, indicating chronic neglect
419 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (262 alterations, 98 new buildings, 15 demolitions) suggesting active construction that may be exacerbating road damage
reporting_angles: Field reporting: document specific street segments with potholes, trenches, or trench restoration failures; identify which streets have highest complaint density
Interview residents about commute impacts and safety concerns; connect to DOT budget constraints or delayed maintenance cycle

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints peaked at 1,718 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 540% surge above the 8-week baseline of 268.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 9.39, highest severity), with no sign of resolution in latest data, suggesting sustained disruption affecting quality of life.
evidence: 1,718 residential noise complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 268.4 weekly average (540% spike, z-score 9.39, highest z-score in dataset)
Vehicle noise complaints also elevated last week at 15 complaints vs. 2.8 baseline (446% increase, z-score 6.17), suggesting concurrent construction/traffic noise
Noise spike timing aligns with active construction activity (98 new building permits, 262 alteration permits filed in 90-day window)
reporting_angles: Identify construction sites, demolition schedules, or special events active 2 weeks ago; cross-reference with DOB permits to pinpoint sources
Interview affected residents on health/sleep impacts; determine if noise complaints are concentrated in specific neighborhoods or building types

themes_detail.label: Sewer System Strain
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints jumped to 20 LAST WEEK, a 371% spike above the 8-week baseline of 4.2 weekly complaints (z-score: 9.19, high severity), matching a long-standing community board request to inspect and repair storm sewers on specific street segments.
evidence: 20 sewer complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly average (371% increase, z-score 9.19)
Community board has repeatedly requested DEP storm sewer inspection and service/repair/replacement on specific street segments (unfunded, recurring request)
Street condition spike (64 complaints THIS WEEK) may indicate related infrastructure failure—sewer backups often manifest as road damage
reporting_angles: Obtain DEP records of which street segments have pending sewer inspections or known defects; determine if reported complaints cluster on those streets
Interview residents experiencing sewage backups or street flooding; assess public health risk and whether repairs have been deferred

themes_detail.label: Damaged Tree Surge
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints jumped to 11 THIS WEEK, a 363% spike above the 8-week baseline of 2.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 4.99), coinciding with community board's recurring request for new Parks Department maintenance equipment.
evidence: 11 damaged tree complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly average (363% increase, z-score 4.99)
Parks Department maintenance equipment request appears as standing unfunded budget priority, suggesting chronic under-resourcing
Spike may reflect recent weather event or storm damage, or indicate delayed response to damaged trees due to equipment/staffing constraints
reporting_angles: Determine if spike followed recent storm event or high winds; cross-reference with weather data from this week
Interview Parks Department about equipment backlog and tree maintenance response times; assess whether new equipment funding could accelerate repairs

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints reached 3 LAST WEEK, a 1,100% spike above the 8-week baseline of 0.2 weekly complaints (z-score: 6.35), suggesting a sudden wave of graffiti or illegal signage that warrants investigation.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,100% increase, z-score 6.35)
Baseline is extremely low (0.2 per week), making any uptick statistically pronounced; outbreak may be localized to specific area or campaign
Data does not clarify whether postings are political, commercial, or gang-related, requiring field verification
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to determine if postings are concentrated in specific neighborhood blocks; identify type and content of illegal postings
Assess whether this represents new gang activity, political campaign overflow, or a one-week anomaly that has already resolved
